SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبرجلحسنأبواهوأحسنأب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبرجلحسنأبواهوأحسنأب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبرجلحسنأبواهوأحسنأب.claim: Stars, celestial bodies, and ants receive rational plural treatment when portrayed as obeying, understanding, or being worshipped; Sībawayh cites 21:33, 12:4, and 27:18, and explains the personification.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبرجلحسنأبواهوأحسنأب.anchor: حين ~~حدثت عنه كما تحدث عن الأناسى

ITQAN:v3p249/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p249/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p249/r5.claim: A further type is a word readable the same forward and backward; the Quran’s only examples are كل في فلك and وربك فكبر.
ITQAN:v3p249/r5.anchor: ومنه نوع يسمى القلب والمقلوب المستوى وما لا يستحيل بالانعكاس وهو أن تقرأ الكلمة من آخرها إلى أولها كما تقرأ من أولها إلى آخرها

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r5.claim: The universe's evident signs already attest to God's providence, mercy, wisdom, justice, monotheism, and the Day of Judgement, so no new sign is needed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r5.anchor: why do they not reflect on the ones which are present before them all the time

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r8.claim: In كل يسبحون the nunation compensates for an omitted annexed noun; فلك is the circular body or course of day and night.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r8.anchor: والتنوين في كل عوض من المضاف إليه، والفلك الجسم الدائر دورة اليوم والليلة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi explain الفلك as the sky.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r9.anchor: وعن ابن عباس والسدي: الفلك السماء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r10.claim: Most commentators call الفلك a contained wave beneath the sky; Qatada describes it as a circular orbit between heaven and earth while the sky stays fixed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r10.anchor: وقال أكثر المفسرين: الفلك موج مكفوف تحت السماء تجري فيه الشمس والقمر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r11.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r11.claim: Other reports identify the orbit as the pole, an orbit particular to each planet, or an immaterial track; al-Dahhak says it is not a body.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r11.anchor: وقال الضحاك: الفلك ليس بجسم وإنما هو مدار هذه النجوم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r12.claim: The apparent view is that the orbit is a body and every celestial object swims in one orbit; another view assigns each its own.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p426/r12.anchor: والظاهر أنه جسم وفيه الاختلاف المذكور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p427/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p427/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p427/r1.claim: The plural verb يسبحون may imply an omitted coordinated “stars”; without an omitted plural, the verb would be dual.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p427/r1.anchor: فقيل ثم معطوف محذوف وهو والنجوم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p427/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p427/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p427/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari makes the pronoun refer to the sun and moon as recurring classes of risings, metaphorically pluralized despite each being one.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p427/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p427/r3.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p427/r3.claim: Al-Farra’ says the masculine intelligent plural is used because swimming is an action associated with people; al-Razi reports Ibn Sina’s view that the bodies themselves reason.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p427/r3.anchor: لما كانت السباحة من أفعال الآدميين جاء ما أسند إليهما مجموعا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p427/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p427/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p427/r4.claim: The clause may be independent or circumstantial of sun and moon; night and day cannot be the objects moving in an orbit, which itself does not move.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p427/r4.anchor: والذي يدل عليه الظاهر أن الشمس والقمر هما اللذان يجريان في الفلك

SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r1.claim: كل may refer to the two nearer antecedents, sun and moon, or to all four named bodies: night, day, sun, and moon.
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r1.anchor: أي: من الشمس والقمر، أو منها أي: من الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر.

SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r2.claim: يسبحون can be the predicate of كل according to its meaning; في فلك then attaches to it.
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r2.anchor: و " يسبحون " يجوز أن يكون خبر " كل " على المعنى. و " في فلك " متعلق به،

SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r3.claim: Alternatively, في فلك is the predicate and يسبحون is a circumstantial clause.
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r3.anchor: وهذا الذي: ذكرته من كون المضاف إليه يجوز أن يقدر بالأربعة الأشياء المذكورة.

SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows the genitive complement of كل to be any of the four named entities, while others specify only sun and moon.
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r4.anchor: ذكره أبو البقاء. وأما غيره فلم يذكر إلا أن المضاف إليه الشمس والقمر.

SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r5.claim: The author prefers sun and moon as the referents, since swimming is their characteristic rather than that of night and day.
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r5.anchor: السباحة من صفتهما دون الليل والنهار، وعلى هذا فيعتذر عن الإتيان بضمير الجمع

SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r6.claim: If all four are included, their plural may be explained by an omitted conjunct, the stars, which other verses indicate.
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r6.anchor: أما الأول فقيل: إنما جمع لأن ثم معطوفا محذوفا تقديره: والنجوم، كما دلت

SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the pronoun refers to the sun and moon as the many celestial bodies rising over successive days and nights, which explains plural suns and moons.
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r7.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " الضمير للشمس والقمر، والمراد بهما جنس الطوالع كل يوم وليلة،

SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r8.claim: The verse ending helps make the plural wording suitable.
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r8.anchor: والذي حسن ذلك كونه رأس آية.

SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r9.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r9.claim: Abu al-Baqa says the plural is the predicate of كل by sense, since if each one swims then all swim; it can instead be circumstantial with في فلك as predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r9.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " يسبحون " خبر " كل " على المعنى؛ لأن كل واحد إذا سبح فكلها تسبح.

SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r10.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r10.claim: Abu al-Baqa also supplies كلها as the subject and makes يسبحون its predicate; the author finds a mismatch between the plural predicate and its circumstantial subject if all four antecedents are intended.
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r10.anchor: أتى بضمير الجمع على معنى " كل ". وفي هذا الكلام نظر: من حيث إنه لما جوز

SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r11.claim: Attributing swimming, an action of rational beings, to the bodies permits a rational masculine plural; examples are cited from Joseph and Fussilat.
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r11.anchor: لما أسند إليها السباحة التي هي من أفعال العقلاء جمعها جمع العقلاء

SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r12.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r12.claim: The Shaykh takes the clause as circumstantial only of sun and moon, since night and day are not described as running in an orbit; al-Zamakhshari had already used the same example.
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r12.anchor: من الشمس والقمر؛ لأن الليل والنهار لا يتصفان بأنهما يجريان في فلك، فهو كقولك

SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r13.claim: The sentence may be independent with no syntactic position or accusative as a circumstantial clause; the latter can refer to all four entities if night and day swim, or just sun and moon otherwise.
SAMIN-DURR:21:33/r13.anchor: وهذه الجملة يجوز أن تكون لا محل لها من الإعراب لاستئنافها. ويجوز أن يكون محلها النصب على الحال.

SAMIN-DURR:21:33#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:33#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:33#2/r1.claim: Swimming is literally movement through water and can also express going generally; its derivation was treated earlier under سبحانك.
SAMIN-DURR:21:33#2/r1.anchor: والسباحة: العوم في الماء. وقد يعبر به عن مطلق الذهاب، وقد تقدم اشتقاقه

ZAJJAJ:v3p391/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p391/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p391/r3.claim: The plural يسبحون is used of the sun, moon, night, and day as though rational because they are described by action, like the Arab expression أكلوني البراغيث.
ZAJJAJ:v3p391/r3.anchor: قيل يسبحون كما يقال لما يعقل، لأن هذه الأشياء وصفت بالفعل كما يوصف من يعقل،

ZAJJAJ:v3p391/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p391/r4.speaker: الشاعر
ZAJJAJ:v3p391/r4.claim: The poet's line about بنو نعش is cited as evidence for plural agreement with nonhuman referents.
ZAJJAJ:v3p391/r4.anchor: قال الشاعر: شربت بها والديك يدعو صباحه. . . إذا ما بنو نعش دنوا فتصوبوا

ASAD-NOTES:21:31/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:31/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:31/r3.claim: God created night, day, sun, and moon, all of which float through space.
ASAD-NOTES:21:31/r3.anchor: and [fail to see that] it is He who has created the night and th e day

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r2.claim: The night, day, sun, and moon complement one another in harmony, showing that one governing intelligence made them serve the world’s collective benefit.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r2.anchor: they are complementing one another and are in total harmony with one another. This is evidence enough to show that this universe is being government by a single mind

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r3.claim: Kull here refers to the sun and moon; in this construction it identifies a noun already mentioned, whether there are two or more referents.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r3.anchor: When the word w (each) occurs in this way, it becomes an instrument for defining a noun and refers to it as mentioned regardless of being two or more.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r4.claim: The sun and moon keep their prescribed paths with minute precision; deviation would disrupt the universe, proving their submission to its master.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r4.anchor: They follow their course with minute precision and continue to do so with this perfection. This bears evidence to the fact that they obey the master of this universe.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r5.claim: Demanding another sign despite obvious celestial signs is foolish, and worshipping the sun or moon is especially so because they visibly submit.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r5.anchor: Even worse are those who have regarded the sun and the moon as deities even though they by their very existence continuously show that they are submissive.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r6.claim: The opponents mock the Prophet’s humanity and status and demand a proof of his messengership; the signs of 21:30–33 answer that demand.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p113/r6.anchor: how can he be God’s messenger when he is a human being; he also has no distinction over them in wealth and status.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p23#6/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p23#6/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p23#6/r1.claim: Qatada says the celestial bodies move through the sky’s orbit, as one can see.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p23#6/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ في فلك يسبحون ﴾ قال يجرون في فلك السماء كما رأيت

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p23#6/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p23#6/r2.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p23#6/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says anything that revolves is a falak, or orbit.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p23#6/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي كل شيء يدور فهو فلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p403#3/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p403#3/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p403#3/r9.claim: The root سبح means swimming or floating through water.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p403#3/r9.anchor: السبح: العوم، كلأه: حفظه يكلؤه كلاءة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r1.claim: The sun and moon are the signs of night and day; their mention illustrates the preceding signs, with a shift of address that emphasizes the discourse’s point.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r1.anchor: اللذين هما آيتاهما ولذا لم يعد الفعل بيانا لبعض تلك الآيات

ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r2.speaker: some commentators
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r2.claim: Some explain the choice of jaʿala for the sky and khalaqa here by saying night and day are not produced like animals or mountains; al-Alusi calls this explanation unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r2.anchor: ولما كان إيجاد الليل والنهار ليس على نمط إيجاد الحيوانات وإيجاد الرواسي

ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r3.claim: Kull is the subject, with its tanwīn standing in for a genitive complement; al-Zamakhshari takes the implied complement as the singular indefinite “each one of the sun and moon.”
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r3.anchor: مبتدأ وتنوينه عوض عن المضاف إليه واعتبره صاحب الكشاف

ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r4.speaker: ابن هشام
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r4.claim: Ibn Hisham objects that if kull’s omitted complement is singular indefinite, its agreeing pronoun must also be singular; the plural verb instead requires construing the complement as a plural definite, with agreement revealing the omitted form.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r4.anchor: قد صرح ابن هشام في المغنى بأن المقدر إذا كان مفردا نكرة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan allows either singular or plural agreement regardless of how the omitted complement of kull is construed, permitting al-Zamakhshari’s analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r5.anchor: وأبو حيان يجوز الإفراد والجمع مطلقا فيجوز هنا اعتبار المضاف إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r6.claim: Fī falak is the predicate; its singular form suits kull’s distributive, indefinite sense of each one, rather than a collective sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r6.anchor: خبره ووجه إفراده ظاهر لأن النكرة المقدرة للعموم البدلي لا الشمولي

ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r7.claim: If kull is taken as a plural generic, the phrase means each belongs to its own orbit, since sun and moon do not together occupy one orbit.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r7.anchor: ومن قدر جمعا معرفا قال : المراد به الجنس الكلي المؤل بالجمع

ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r8.claim: Yasbaḥūn may be a circumstantial clause or a predicate, with fī falak then functioning circumstantially or as its complement; the whole kull clause can modify sun and moon without a conjunction, or be taken as a new sentence.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r8.anchor: حال ويجوز أن يكون الخبر و ( في فلك ) حالا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r9.claim: The plural pronoun can reflect the many apparent rising points of the sun and moon, allowing figurative plural forms despite one of each in reality.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r9.anchor: وكان ضميرهما جمعا اعتبارا للتكثير بتكاثر المطالع

ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r10.claim: Another explanation says the two luminaries receive a plural pronoun by honorific precedence; others take it to refer to stars, or also to sun, moon, night, and day, though the latter is unsuitable because night and day do not swim even figuratively.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r10.anchor: وفيه أن الليل والنهار لا يحسن وصفهما بالسباحة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r11.claim: Rational plural agreement is explained either by the view of some Muslims that the celestial bodies are actually rational or by treating them as rational because swimming is normally an act of rational agents.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r11.anchor: واختيار ضمير العقلاء إما لأنهما عقلاء حقيقية كما ذهب

ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r12.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r12.claim: Falak originally denotes any round, revolving object, as in the spindle’s whorl; Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi identify the orbit here as the heaven.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p39/r12.anchor: والفلك في الأصل كل شيء دائر ومنه فلكه المغزل

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r1.claim: Most commentators identify the falak as a contained wave beneath the heaven in which the sun and moon travel.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r1.anchor: وقال أكثر المفسرين : هو موج مكفوف تحت السماء

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r2.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says the falak is not a body but the orbit of the stars.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r2.anchor: وقال الضحاك : هو ليس بجسم وإنما هو مدار هذه النجوم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r3.claim: The well-known transmitted interpretation from Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi is that falak means heaven, implying that heaven is spherical; al-Alusi finds a subtle hint of this in the distributive wording, and says its being a roof does not rule it out.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r3.anchor: والمشهور ما روي عن ابن عباس والسدي وفيه القول باستدارة السماء

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r4.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r4.claim: Philosophers describe each celestial sphere as living, knowing, volitionally moving only in a circle, imperishable, indivisible, and without the ordinary elemental qualities or tendencies.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r4.anchor: في كلام الفلاسفة إطلاق الفلك على السماء ووصوفه بأنه حي عالم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r5.claim: Kalam theologians reject many of these philosophical claims; philosophers infer multiple spheres from the impossibility of celestial rupture and differing planetary motions, and commonly posit nine in all.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r5.anchor: وقد رد ذلك في الكتب الكلامية وبنوا على امتناع الخرق والالتئام

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r6.claim: The standard philosophical scheme assigns seven spheres to the wandering planets, one to fixed stars, and one outer sphere to impart daily motion to all.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r6.anchor: والمشهور أن الأفلاك الكلية تسعة سبعة للسبع السيارة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r7.claim: Al-Alusi says there is no decisive proof that no additional spheres exist; even Avicenna was unsure whether fixed stars occupy one sphere or nested spheres.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r7.anchor: والحق أنه لا قاطع على نفي ما عدا ذلك ألا ترى أن الشيخ الرئيس

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r8.claim: The claim that similar apparent stellar motions prove the stars occupy one sphere is uncertain: observations may conceal tiny differences, such as rotations taking 36,000 years versus slightly less.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r8.anchor: وقولهم إن حركات الثوابت متشابهة ومتى كانت كذلك كانت مركوزة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r9.claim: The source adds that later astronomers found Herschel, whose motion is faster than the fixed stars’ but slower than the visible planets’, unknown to earlier observers.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r9.anchor: وجدان المتأخرين من أهل الأرصاد كوكبا أسرع حركة من الثوابت

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r10.claim: The inference that objects with similar motions share one sphere is not conclusive, since distinct things can share properties; separate spheres could move in the same direction and share poles and other dimensions.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r10.anchor: وأما كبراه فلا احتمال اشتراك الأشياء المختلفة في كثير من اللوازم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r11.claim: Additional spheres could lie between planetary spheres; the geometric objection based on equal nearest and farthest distances fails because epicycles and the lunar node sphere can intervene.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r11.anchor: بل حاصل في كل الأفلاك فيجوز أن يكون بين أفلاك السيارة أفلاك أخر

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r12.claim: Astronomers posit several epicycle spheres for each superior planet and five for inferior planets; assuming adjacent spheres touch because no interposed sphere exists is circular, so another proof is needed.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40/r12.anchor: ذكر المحققون من أصحاب الهيئة أن لفلك التدوير لكل من العلوية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r1.claim: The number and nesting of celestial spheres may exceed the familiar nine; the larger Martian circle than the Sun's demonstrates that still larger nested structures are conceivable.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r1.anchor: ويجوز أيضا أن يكون فوق التاسع من الأفلاك ما لا يعلمه إلا الله تعالى بل يحتمل

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r2.claim: One model has eight whole spheres, with fixed stars on the outer convex of Saturn's deferent and the eighth sphere accounting for the other motion.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r2.anchor: أن تكون الأفلاك الكلية ثمانية لا مكان كون جميع الثوابت مركوزة في محدب ممثل زحل

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r3.claim: Another proposed seven-sphere model places fixed stars and zodiac circles on Saturn's deferent and assigns the two motions to separate rotations.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r3.anchor: بل قيل من الجائز أن تكون سبعة بأن تفرض الثوابت ودوائر البروج على محدب ممثل زحل

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r4.claim: There is no decisive proof that the celestial spheres must number nine rather than fewer.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r4.anchor: فلا قاطع أيضا على نفي أن تكون الأفلاك أقل من تسعة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r5.claim: The verse apparently says that the Sun and Moon each travel within the thickness of its own sphere; reason supplies no obstacle to this.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r5.anchor: ثم الظاهر من الآية أن كلا من الشمس والقمر يجري في ثخن فلكه ولا مانع منه عقلا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r6.claim: The usual proof that spheres cannot be pierced because they would then admit straight motion is incomplete, and even if sound applies only to the outermost sphere.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r6.anchor: ودليل امتناع الخرق والإلتئام وهو أنه لو كان الفلك قابلا لذلك لكان قابلا للحركة المستقيمة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r7.claim: Stars could move through their spheres like fish through water; uniform motion around each sphere's center would preserve astronomy's observed calculations.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r7.anchor: الكواكب مطلقا متحركة في أفلاكها حركة الحيتان في الماء ولا يبطل به علم الهيئة لأن حركاتها يلزم أن تكون متشابهة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r8.speaker: السهروردي
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r8.claim: Suhrawardi argues that a living sphere pierced and dispersed by a planet would either lack awareness of its parts or feel pain from the injury, implying endless torment.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r8.anchor: لو كانت الأفلاك قابلة للخرق وقد برهن على كونها ذات حياة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r9.claim: Al-Alusi dismisses Suhrawardi's argument as mere rhetoric, below even that standard, rather than a demonstration.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r9.anchor: لا يخفى أنه من الخطابيات بل مما هو أدون منها

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r10.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r10.claim: Some call the anti-piercing argument a powerful proof, but al-Alusi says it has no proof behind it and is weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r10.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أنه من البراهين القوية مما لا برهان عليه من البراهين الضعيفة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r11.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r11.claim: The Imam claims the verse indicates both a planet's motion and the sphere's rest.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r11.anchor: وادعى الإمام أنها كما تدل على جري الكوكب تدل على سكون الفلك

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r12.claim: Al-Alusi says the verse is ambiguous about whether the sphere rests and does not clearly establish sphere motion either.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r12.anchor: والحق أنها مجملة بالنسبة إلى السكون غير ظاهرة فيه وإلى حركته وسكون الفلك بأسره

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r13.speaker: بعض المسلمين والشيخ الأكبر
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r13.claim: Some Muslims, and reportedly Ibn Arabi, hold that the sphere as a whole moves.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r13.anchor: وإلى حركته وسكون الفلك بأسره ذهب بعض المسلمين ويحكى عن الشيخ الأكبر

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r14.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r14.claim: Alternatives include a moving sphere with its planet moving alongside or against it at equal or differing speeds, or a planet fixed in the sphere or spinning on itself while the whole sphere moves; al-Alusi says the philosophers' required model lacks proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r14.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الفلك متحركا والكوكب يتحرك فيه إما مخالفا لجهة حركته أو موافقا لها

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r15.claim: A planet might instead occupy a separate moving ring-like body, about its own diameter, while the main sphere remains still.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r15.anchor: ويجوز أيضا أن يكون الكوكب في جسم منفصل عن ثخن الفلك شبيه بحلقة قطره مساو لقطر الكوكب

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r16.claim: A hollow track in a resting or moving sphere could carry the planet without piercing the sphere; this entails a vacuum, which al-Alusi and most philosophers allow against Aristotle and his followers.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r16.anchor: ويجوز أيضا أن يكون في ثخن الفلك خلاء يدور الكوكب فيه مع سكون الفلك أو حركته وليس في هذا قول بالخرق والإلتئام

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r17.claim: A sphere's simplicity does not rule out hollowness: arguments for simplicity are weak and apply only to the outermost sphere, and hollow structures can be posited within a simple sphere.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r17.anchor: فما ذكروه من الدليل على البساطة على ضعفه لا يتأتى إلا في المحدد دون سائر الأفلاك

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r18.claim: A report says all stars hang from chains of light beneath the lowest heaven, pulled by angels as God wills; al-Alusi doubts its soundness while affirming God's power over all things.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r18.anchor: وجاء في بعض الآثار أن الكواكب جميعها معلقة بسلاسل من نور تحت سماء الدنيا بأيدي ملائكة يجرونها حيث شاء الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r19.speaker: الفلاسفة والهيئيون
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r19.claim: Most philosophers and astronomers assign planets a slow intrinsic west-to-east zodiacal motion, obvious in planets and the Moon but subtle in fixed stars, plus a fast east-to-west carried motion from the outer sphere that causes day and night; near latitude 90 the slower motion governs instead.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r19.anchor: والذي عليه معظم الفلاسفة والهيئيين أن الحركة الخاصة بالكوكب الثابتة لفلكه أولا وبالذات آخذة من المغرب إلى المشرق

ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r20.claim: The two opposing motions are illustrated by a mill turning quickly one way and an ant crawling slowly across it the other way.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p40#2/r20.anchor: ومثلوهما بحركة رحى إلى جهة سريعا وحركة نملة عليها إلى خلاف تلك الجهة بطيئا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p42/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42/r1.speaker: بعض الأوائل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42/r1.claim: Some ancients deny any celestial west-to-east motion, arguing that east-to-west better suits the heavenly bodies because it is less contrary to their nature.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42/r1.anchor: وذهب بعض الأوائل إلى أنه لا حركة في الأجرام العلوية من المغرب إلى المشرق بل حركاتها كلها من المشرق إلى المغرب لأنها أولى بهذه الأجرام

ALUSI-FULL:v17p42/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42/r2.speaker: بعض الأوائل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42/r2.claim: They argue that motion is greatest at the outermost sphere and rest greatest at Earth, so bodies nearer the outermost sphere should move faster than those farther away.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42/r2.anchor: ولأن غاية الحركة للجرم الأقصى وغاية السكون للأرض فيجب أن يكون ما هو أقرب إلى الأقصى أسرع

ALUSI-FULL:v17p42/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42/r3.speaker: بعض الأوائل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42/r3.claim: They also argue that one body cannot move in opposite directions simultaneously: each motion would require the body to occupy a different place at once, whether the motions are natural, forced, or mixed.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42/r3.anchor: ولأنه كان بعضها من المشرق وبعضها من المغرب يلزم أن يتحرك الكوكب بحركتين مختلفتين جهة وذلك محال

ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r1.claim: The ant-on-a-mill example does not refute the impossibility argument: an example cannot invalidate a proof, and such paired motions may be possible on Earth but not in celestial spheres.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r1.anchor: ولا يدفع هذا بما شاهد من حركة النملة على الرحى إلى جهة حال حركة الرحى إلى خلافها لأنه مثال والمثال لا يقدح في البرهان

ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r2.claim: Apparent westward displacement need not be actual: two bodies moving circularly in the same direction appear to move oppositely when the slower one falls behind the faster.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r2.anchor: لجواز أن تكون من المشرق ويظن أنها من المغرب وبيانه أن المتحركين إلى جهة واحدة حركة دورية متى كان أحدهما أسرع

ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r3.speaker: بعض الأوائل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r3.claim: The ancients say proof requires their single-direction account and that astronomical observations do not disprove it.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r3.anchor: وقالوا : يجب المصير إلى ذلك لما أن البرهان يقتضيه ولا يبطله شيء من الأعمال النجومية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r4.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r4.claim: In al-Mulakhkhas the Imam raises the impossibility of opposite motions as an objection to those affirming them; its force led some to posit Earth's daily rotation, which al-Alusi says is false, while the Imam's tafsir calls the argument decisive and adopts the all-east-to-west view.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r4.anchor: وقد أورد الإمام في الملخص ما ذكر في الإستدلال على محالية الحركتين المختلفتي الجهة للجسم الواحد إشكالا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r5.claim: Al-Alusi says the first two arguments are merely persuasive; although the third sounds demonstrative, observations show its proposed trajectories are false.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r5.anchor: وفيما ذكروه نظر لأن الشبهتين الأوليين إقناعيتان والثالثة وإن كانت برهانية لكن فسادها أظهر من أن يخفى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r6.claim: The Moon's residual daily path cannot fit the zodiacal poles or celestial-equator poles: those alternatives would produce paths parallel to the equator rather than the observed large circle crossing it.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r6.anchor: لا يجوز أن تكون على قطبي البروج لأنها توجد موازية لمعدل النهار ولا على قطبي المعدل وإلا لما زالت على موازاته

ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r7.claim: Other pole choices would yield the wrong visible arcs and fail to bisect rising-to-setting time at the meridian; the Sun would also reach all its extreme distances and northern and southern positions in one day, contrary to observation.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p42#2/r7.anchor: ولأنه لو كان الأمر كما توهموا لكانت الشمس تصل إلى أوجها وحضيضها وبعديها الأوسطين بل إلى الشمال والجنوب

ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r1.claim: The Sun cannot move westward along the zodiac: that would shorten each day below the equator's rotation, whereas observation shows the day is longer by the Sun's daily arc; it also traverses signs in the wrong order.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r1.anchor: لكان اليوم الواحد بليلته ينقص عن دور معدل النهار بقدر القوس التي قطعتها الشمس بالتقريب بخلاف ما هو الواقع

ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r2.claim: Because the Sun lags eastward behind the equatorial point sharing its meridian, enclosing spheres have motions in both directions: with and against zodiacal order.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r2.anchor: لتأخرها عن الجزء الذي يتوسط معها من المعدل في كل يوم نحو المشرق فإذا حركات الأفلاك الشاملة للأرض ثنتان

ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r3.claim: Epicycle motions are outside the two classes of Earth-enclosing rotations: an epicycle's top and bottom necessarily move oppositely, for superior planets and for the Moon alike.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r3.anchor: وأما حركات التداوير فخارجة عن القسمين لأن حركات أعاليها مخالفة لحركات أسافلها لا محالة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r4.claim: The philosophers' detailed account of celestial spheres and their motions is possible but not proven to be actual or exclusive; modern London observers and Ibn Arabi's spiritual observations hold otherwise, as discussed in the Futuhat.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r4.anchor: إن ما ذكره الفلاسفة في أمر الأفلاك الكلية والجزئية وكيفية حركتها وأوضاعها أمر ممكن في نفسه ولا دليل على أنه هو الواقع لا غير

ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r5.claim: The early righteous generations did not transmit detailed cosmologies because they had little practical value; they stopped at sound reports and submitted to God's decree where causes were hidden.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r5.anchor: وأما السلف الصالح فلم يصح عنهم تفصيل الكلام في ذلك لما أنه قليل الجدوى ووقفوا حيث صح الخبر

ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r6.claim: Al-Alusi inclines to heavens structured as sound Prophetic reports describe their thickness and intervening distances; a planet's sphere could lie within each heaven and combine its own motion with that heaven's westward daily motion.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r6.anchor: والذي أميل إليه أن السماوات على طبق ما صحت به الأخبار النبوية في أمر الثخن وما بين كل سماء وسماء

ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r7.claim: If reports preclude an entire heaven moving with all it contains, one may posit an inner mover that moves some portions while others remain still, with angels glorifying God on the upper surface.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r7.anchor: يجوز أن يكون هناك محرك في ثخن السماء أيضا ويبقى ما يبقى منها ساكنا بقدرة الله تعالى على سطحه الأعلى ملائكة يسبحون الليل والنهار

ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r8.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r8.claim: Al-Razi says God by choice is the mover of the whole; even on the philosophers' account of an encompassing sphere moving what it contains, it does so through its own power rather than contact.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r8.anchor: الصحيح أن المحرك للكل هو الله تعالى باختياره وإن ثبت على قانون قولهم كون الحاوي محركا للمحوي

ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r9.claim: The fixed stars may be in a sphere above the seven heavens, or within the seventh heaven above Saturn's sphere.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r9.anchor: وأما الثوابت فيحتمل أن تكون في فلم فوق السماوات السبع

ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r10.claim: It is also possible that fixed and wandering stars all lie in the lowest heaven, each on a deferent-like sphere with the two motions, preserving the wording that the lowest heaven is adorned with lamps.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r10.anchor: بل إذا قيل بأن جميع الكواكب الثوابت والسيارات في ثخن السماء الدنيا تتحرك على أفلاك مماثلة للأفلاك التي أثبتها لها الفلاسفة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r11.claim: Al-Alusi is not obliged to accept the confused astronomical measurements of celestial sizes and distances.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r11.anchor: وما ذكروه في علم الأجرام والأبعاد على اضطرابه لا يلزمنا تسليمه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r12.claim: The calculated fixed-star distance of 25,412,899 farsakhs conflicts with reports assigning 500 years to the Earth-heaven gap and each heaven's thickness, which imply roughly 1,000 years plus Earth's radius to the stars.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p43/r12.anchor: وما ورد في الخبر من أن بين السماء والأرض خمسمائة عام وسمك السماء كذلك يقتضي أن يكون بين وجه الأرض والثوابت

ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r1.claim: Al-Alusi says the reported 500 years needs no nonliteral reading: five is a cyclic number and may subtly symbolize circularity, as in every sphere.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r1.anchor: واختيار خمسمائة لما أن الخمسة عدد دائر

ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas compares the Sun to a waterwheel moving through its sphere in the sky, then through its sphere beneath Earth at night until sunrise; the Moon behaves likewise.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال

ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r3.claim: Many transmitted reports concern the stars, heavens, and Earth; al-Suyuti collected examples in a treatise on the sunni cosmology, and al-Alusi judges most outside the bounds of acceptability.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r3.anchor: والأخبار المرفوعة والموقوفة في أمر الكواكب والسماوات والأرض كثيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r4.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r4.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir transmits from Ikrima that the Sun does not rise until ordered, as though a bow were drawn, suggesting its motion is compelled.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r4.anchor: نحو ما أخرجه ابن المنذر عن عكرمة ما طلعت الشمس حتى يؤمر لها كما توتر القوس

ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r5.claim: The apparent sense of swimming is a star's own, intrinsic motion.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r5.anchor: ثم الظاهر أن يراد بالسباحة الحركة الذاتية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r6.claim: Others allow the word to mean the carried, apparent motion and consider this likelier because it is visible, whereas intrinsic motion is unknown to ordinary people.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بها الحركة العرضية بل قيل هذا أولى لأن تلك غير مشاهدة مشاهدة هذه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r7.claim: A further view takes swimming to encompass both kinds of celestial motion.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r7.anchor: وقيل يجوز أن يراد بها ما يعم الحركتين

ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r8.claim: Some infer from calling the star a swimmer that it is not carried by a body moving with it, but swims through its sphere like a fish through water; al-Alusi favors a passage capable of rupture and rejoining, without proving that impossible.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p44/r8.anchor: واستنبط بعضهم من نسبة السباحة إلى الكوكب أن ليس هناك حامل له يتحرك بحركته مطلقا بل هو متحرك بنفسه في الفلك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r4.claim: The celestial bodies run swiftly like swimmers; the rational plural is used because their motion is described as an action of rational beings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r4.anchor: يجرون ويسيرون بسرعة كالسابح في الماء، وإنما قال: {يسبحون} ولم يقل يسبح

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r5.claim: A falak is the circuit containing the stars; in Arabic it can mean any round thing, and its plural is aflāk, as in the spindle’s whorl.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r5.anchor: والفلك في كلام العرب: كل شيء مستدير، وجمعه أفلاك، ومنه فلك المغزل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r6.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan likens the falak to a mill or spindle whorl: the course of the stars is round like a millstone.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن: الفلك طاحونة كهيئة فلكة المغزل: يريد أن الذي يجري فيه النجوم مستدير كاستدارة الطاحونة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r7.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r7.claim: Another view, identified as Qatāda’s meaning, says each star runs in the heaven assigned to it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم: الفلك السماء الذي فيه ذلك الكوكب، فكل كوكب يجري في السماء الذي قدر فيه، وهو معنى قول قتادة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r8.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r8.claim: Al-Kalbī says the falak is the heaven’s circular form.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r9.claim: Another group says the falak is a contained wave beneath the heaven in which the sun, moon, and stars travel.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p317/r9.anchor: وقال آخرون: الفلك موج مكفوف دون السماء يجري فيه الشمس والقمر والنجوم (2)

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:33-34/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:33-34/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:33-34/r1.claim: The created night and day and courses of sun and moon further explain the signs just mentioned.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:33-34/r1.anchor: بيان لبعض تلك الآيات. { كل فى فلك } أي كل واحد منهما

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:33-34/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:33-34/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:33-34/r2.claim: Each is meant; the tanwīn stands in place of a genitive complement, and falak is generic singular, like a prince clothing people in a garment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:33-34/r2.anchor: أي كل واحد منهما، والتنوين بدل من المضاف إليه والمراد بالفلك الجنس

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:33-34/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:33-34/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:33-34/r3.claim: They move swiftly along the orbit's surface like a swimmer moving over water.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:33-34/r3.anchor: يسرعون على سطح الفلك إسراع السابح على سطح الماء

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:33-34/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:33-34/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:33-34/r4.claim: Yasbaḥūn is the predicate of kull and the sentence circumstantial to sun and moon; plural agreement reflects multiple risings, and the rational plural pronoun is used because swimming is their action.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:33-34/r4.anchor: وهو خبر { كل } والجملة حال من { الشمس والقمر } ، وجاز انفرادهما بها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r7.claim: God alone created night and day and their signs, the sun that gives rise to day and the moon that marks night; naming the greatest signs also implies the other stars.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r8.claim: All the named celestial bodies each swim in the orbit appointed for them; the masculine rational plural pronoun is used by grammatical predominance.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p81/r8.anchor: أي كل واحد يسبح في الفلك الذي جعل به

DURR-FULL:v5p627/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r3.claim: A report says Jews asked the Prophet what Friday was; he answered that God created night and day during two of its hours.
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة أن اليهود قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما يوم الجمعة قال: خلق الله في ساعتين منه الليل والنهار

DURR-FULL:v5p627/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses falak as rotation and يسبحون as moving along.
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {كل في فلك} قال: دوران {يسبحون} قال: يجرون

DURR-FULL:v5p627/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas compares the orbit to a spindle's whorl: heavenly bodies revolve in their courses as the whorl turns on the spindle.
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {كل في فلك} قال: فلكة كفلكة المغزل {يسبحون} قال: يدورون في أبواب السماء

DURR-FULL:v5p627/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies the falak as the heaven's orbit.
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {كل في فلك} قال: هو فلك السماء

DURR-FULL:v5p627/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r7.speaker: حسان بن عطية
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r7.claim: Hassan ibn Atiyya says the sun, moon, and stars are subjected to an orbit between heaven and earth.
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r7.anchor: عن حسان بن عطية قال: الشمس والقمر والنجوم مسخرة في فلك بين السماء والأرض

DURR-FULL:v5p627/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd locates the falak between heaven and earth in the paths of the stars, sun, and moon, and glosses يسبحون as moving along.
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r8.anchor: عن ابن زيد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {كل في فلك} قال: الفلك الذي بين السماء والأرض من مجاري النجوم والشمس والقمر وفي قوله: {يسبحون} قال: يجرون

DURR-FULL:v5p627/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r9.speaker: الكلبي
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r9.claim: Al-Kalbi says anything that revolves is called a falak.
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r9.anchor: عن الكلبي رضي الله عنه قال: كل شيء يدور فهو فلك

DURR-FULL:v5p627/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r10.claim: Mujahid compares falak to a spindle-whorl and a heavenly mechanism to a mill: each part turns in relation to its counterpart; he treats hisban and falak as equivalent, with the mill's axis like the spindle's whorl.
DURR-FULL:v5p627/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {كل في فلك يسبحون}

DURR-FULL:v5p628/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p628/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p628/r1.claim: Mujahid describes the falak as shaped like an iron millstone.
DURR-FULL:v5p628/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {كل في فلك} قال: الفلك كهيئة حديدة الرحى

DURR-FULL:v5p628/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p628/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p628/r2.claim: Qatada glosses the bodies swimming in their orbit as running in the sky's orbit, as one can observe.
DURR-FULL:v5p628/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {كل في فلك يسبحون} قال: يجرون في فلك السماء كما رأيت

DURR-FULL:v5p628/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p628/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p628/r3.claim: Ikrima explains their swimming as circular rotation.
DURR-FULL:v5p628/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه {كل في فلك يسبحون} قال: هو الدوران

DURR-FULL:v5p628/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p628/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p628/r4.claim: Mujahid also compares the falak to a spindle's whorl turning around the spindle.
DURR-FULL:v5p628/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {كل في فلك يسبحون} قال: المغزل قال كما تدور الفلكة في المغزل

DURR-FULL:v5p628/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p628/r5.speaker: عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v5p628/r5.claim: A reading attributed to Abdullah has يعملون, they work, in place of يسبحون.
DURR-FULL:v5p628/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه {كل في فلك يسبحون} قال: وكان عبد الله يقرأ كل في فلك يعملون

DURR-FULL:v5p628/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p628/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p628/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {كل في فلك يسبحون} قال: يجرون

BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r1.claim: Night is the earth's shadow, day the sun's light, the sun a luminous daytime star, and the moon a luminous nighttime star; God alone brought them from nonexistence into existence, showing perfect power and wisdom.
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r1.anchor: الذي هو ظل الأرض {والنهار} الذي هو ضوء الشمس

BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r2.claim: Each refers to the sun and moon separately; in an orbit is its predicate, while swimming is a circumstantial phrase.
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r2.anchor: كل واحد من الشمس والقمر وهو مبتدأ خبره قوله : {فى فلك}

BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r3.claim: Swimming is swift motion through water or air; it is borrowed here for the stars' motion across their orbits.
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r3.anchor: فإن السبح المر السريع في الماء أو في الهواء

BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r4.speaker: شرح التقويم
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r4.claim: One view holds each celestial body fixed within its sphere like a signet set in a ring, immersed like a ball in water; spheres move by will and the stars move incidentally.
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r4.anchor: قال في "شرح التقويم" : كل واحد من الكواكب مركوز في فلك

BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r5.claim: Another literal reading takes the sphere as a wave held back from flowing beneath the sky, in which sun and moon swim like fish; the sphere is a transparent body surrounding the world.
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم أخذا بظاهر الآية : إن الفلك موج مكفوف من السيلان

BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r6.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r6.claim: Al-Raghib defines falak as the course of the celestial bodies, named for its resemblance to a spindle whorl.
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r6.anchor: قال الراغب الفلك مجرى الكواكب وتسميته بذلك لكونه كالفلك

BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r7.speaker: محيى السنة
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r7.claim: Muhyi al-Sunna says falak in Arabic means any round thing; its plural is aflak, as in a spindle whorl.
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r7.anchor: وقال محيى السنة الفلك في كلام العرب كل شيء مستدير جمعه أفلاك ومنه فلكة المغزل

BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r8.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r8.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh lays out three possible motions: a fixed sphere with moving stars, a moving sphere with stars also moving within it, or a moving sphere carrying stationary stars.
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ : اختلف الناس في حركات الكواكب والوجوه الممكنة فيها ثلاثة

BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r9.speaker: الفلاسفة
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r9.claim: The philosophers reject the first two motion models because they would rupture the spheres, and conclude that the spheres move while the stars are fixed in them.
BURSEVI:v5p363#2/r9.anchor: قال الفلاسفة : الرأي الأول باطل لأنه يوجب خرق الفلك وهو محال وكذا الرأي الثاني

BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r1.speaker: الإمام
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r1.claim: The Imam rejects the philosophers' assumption that spheres cannot rupture: all three models are possible and within God's power; the Qur'an's apparent sense is fixed spheres with stars swimming inside them.
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r1.anchor: قال الإمام : واعلم أن مدار هذا الكلام على امتناع الخرق على الأفلاك وهو باطل بل الحق أن الاحتمالات الثلاثة كلها ممكنة

BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r2.claim: Without the sun and moon and their motions producing day, night, heat, cold, and other benefits, the blessings of the created heaven would not be complete.
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r2.anchor: واعلم أنه لو خلق السماء ولم يخلق الشمس والقمر

BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r3.speaker: ابن سينا
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r3.claim: Ibn Sina argues that the celestial bodies are living and rational because the verse says they swim and Joseph's dream describes the stars prostrating; he says the rational plural is used only for rational beings.
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r3.anchor: واحتج أبو علي بن سينا على كون الكواكب أحياء ناطقة

BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r4.claim: The rational plural does not prove that stars are rational: they are given rational pronouns because swimming and prostrating are actions associated with rational beings; the same usage occurs in the command to enter dwellings.
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r4.anchor: والجواب أنه لما أسند إليهم ما هو من أفعال العقلاء وهو السباحة والسجود نزلن منزلة العقلاء

BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r5.speaker: بعض أهل الحقيقة
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r5.claim: Some people of spiritual realization describe the celestial bodies' movers as immaterial, rational celestial souls, separate from bodily matter in essence but connected to the spheres in motion.
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r5.anchor: قال بعض أهل الحقيقة : الأجرام الفلكية هي الأجسام فوق العناصر من الأفلاك والكواكب

BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r6.claim: The discussion answers an objection about rational speech as the human differentia: speech means what proceeds from the heart, not the tongue, and angels, jinn, and parrots have no such heart.
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r6.anchor: والجواب الحق هو ما يجري على الجنان لا ما يجري على اللسان وليس لهم جنان حتى يجري عليه الشيء

BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r7.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r7.claim: Kashifi reads night and day as the contraction and expansion of gnostics: at times majesty overwhelms them with contraction, at others beauty hosts them in expansion and generosity.
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r7.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (در كشف الاسرار آورده كه نزد اهل اشارت شب وروز

BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r8.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r8.claim: Kashifi takes the sun as the person of divine unity, settled through empowerment in the witnessing presence and neither increasing nor decreasing in certainty.
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r8.anchor: آفتاب نشانه صاحب توحيداست بنعمت تمكين در حضرت شهود آراسته نه فزايد ونه كاهد

BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r9.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r9.claim: Kashifi takes the moon as people of changing spiritual states, waxing and waning between the vanishing of unity's light and the full moon of the comprehensive station.
BURSEVI:v5p363#3/r9.anchor: وقمر نشانه اهل تلوين است كاه دركاهش بود وكاه در افزايش زمانى بظهور نور برق وحدت درمحاق نيستى افتد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r1.claim: The definite nominal clause presents creation as a benefaction and restricts it, countering the polytheists' implied claim that idols share in creation and divinity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r1.anchor: سيقت في معرض المنة بصوغها في صيغة الجملة الاسمية المعرفة الجزأين لإفادة القصر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r2.claim: The passage uses 'created' because its lesson and blessing concern these entities themselves, not their being made in a particular state.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r2.anchor: لا في إيجادها على حالة خاصة ، جيء هنا بفعل الخلق لا بفعل الجعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r3.claim: Night's creation is one instance of creating darkness; darkness is absence and precedes existence, while night is earth's shadow as sunlight turns away.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r3.anchor: فإن الظلمة عدم والنور وجودي وهو ضد الظلمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r4.claim: Daylight results from the sun and its rays reaching the earth's illuminated hemisphere, so mentioning the sun after day points to daylight's origin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r4.anchor: فهو بخلق الشمس ومن توجه أشعتها إلى النصف المقابل للأشعة من الكرة الأرضية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r5.claim: The moon is mentioned alongside the sun and as a benefaction that gives people some light during part of the darkness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r5.anchor: وللتذكير بمنة إيجاد ما ينير على الناس بعض النور في بعض أوقات الظلمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r6.claim: The explanatory sentence answers how the celestial bodies move without colliding or appearing out of time: each travels in its own expanse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p59/r6.anchor: سؤالا عن كيفية سيرها وكيف لا يقع لها اصطدام أو يقع منها تخلف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r1.claim: The plural masculine pronoun refers to the sky's signs and specifically the sun and moon; masculine nouns such as moon and planet support its form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r1.anchor: وضمير { يسبحون } عائد إلى عموم آيات السماء وخصوص الشمس والقمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r2.claim: Al-Kashshāf explains that the rational plural continues the personification begun by describing celestial bodies as swimming.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r2.anchor: وقال في ( الكشاف ) : ( إنه روعي فيه وصفها بالسباحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r3.claim: Fī falak is the predicate, kull is the subject, and its nunation replaces an annexed noun; kull is definite in sense and each object has its own orbit.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r4.claim: The swimming clause is circumstantial; swimming is a metaphor for unimpeded travel through spacious paths that do not intersect.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r5.claim: Lexicographers and commentators define falak as a celestial orbit, though Ibn ʿĀshūr notes they do not attest this use in pre-Islamic Arabic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r5.anchor: والفلك فسره أهل اللغة بأنه مدار النجوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r6.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr suspects falak was a Qur'anic term adopted by Muslim scholars, transferred from the circular sea-wave and ultimately the spindle whorl.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r6.anchor: والأظهر أن القرآن نقله من فلك البحر وهو الموج المستدير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r7.claim: The seven-letter phrase reads identically backward and forward, forming a smooth and useful palindrome; 74:3 gives a similar example without the conjunction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r7.anchor: ومن بدائع الإعجاز في هذه الآية أن قوله تعالى : { كل في فلك } فيه محسن بديعي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r8.claim: Al-Sakkākī calls this pattern al-maqlūb al-mustawī, a variety within the category of qalb.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p60/r8.anchor: وهذا النوع سماه السكاكي ( المقلوب المستوي ) وجعله من أصناف نوع سماه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r10.claim: The falak is a revolving body that completes the cycle of day and night; all the named heavenly bodies move within it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r10.anchor: و «الفلك» الجسم الدائر دورة اليوم والليلة فالكل في ذلك سابح متصرف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r11.claim: Some speculated that the orbit is like a mill's iron or a mill; he says such speculation should be avoided, though the orbit is a revolving body.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r11.anchor: فقال بعضهم كحديد الرحى، وقال بعضهم كالطاحونة مما لا ينبغي التسور عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r12.claim: He explains yasbaḥūn as moving and acting freely within the orbit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r12.anchor: ويسبحون معناه يتصرفون، وقالت فرقة «الفلك» موج مكفوف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r13.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r13.claim: Another group understands the falak as a wave held back and takes swimming in its literal sense of floating.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p80#2/r13.anchor: وقالت فرقة «الفلك» موج مكفوف ورأوا قوله يسبحون من السباحة وهو العوم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r1.claim: “Each” refers to the celestial bodies that rise and travel in an orbit.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى كل يعني الطوالع في فلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba defines falak as the orbit enclosing the stars, named for its roundness, like a spindle's whorl; the same root describes a woman's breast as rounded.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة الفلك مدار النجوم الذي يضمها وسماه فلكا لاستدارته ومنه قيل فلكه المغزل وقد فلك ثدي المرأة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r3.speaker: أبو سليمان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r3.claim: Abu Sulayman offers another view: the falak is a circular, water-wheel-like sphere below the sky and above the earth; earth is at its center, and the heavenly bodies travel in it without its rotating them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r3.anchor: وقيل إن الفلك كهيئة الساقية من ماء مستديرة دون السماء وتحت الأرض فالأرض وسطها والشمس والقمر والنجوم والليل والنهار يجرون في الفلك وليس الفلك يديرها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r4.claim: Yasbaḥūn means that the bodies run or move along.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r5.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r5.claim: Al-Farra says the plural masculine verb “they swim” is used because swimming is a human action, as in “I saw them prostrating to me” at 12:4.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p349#3/r5.anchor: قال الفراء لما كانت السباحة من أفعال الآدميين ذكرت بالنون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r6.claim: Night is dark and still while day brings light and ease; each alternately lengthens and shortens.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r6.anchor: هذا في ظلامه وسكونه، وهذا بضيائه وأنسه، يطول هذا تارة ثم يقصر أخرى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r7.claim: The sun and moon each have distinct light, orbit, time, movement, course, and measure.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r7.anchor: هذه لها نور يخصها، وفلك بذاته، وزمان على حدة، وحركة وسير خاص

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r8.claim: The phrase means they revolve; the verse also links to 36:40 and God's calculation of night and day and the sun and moon in 6:96.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid compare the celestial bodies' rotation to a spindle turning in its whorl, with each turning in relation to the other.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p340#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يدورون كما يدور المغزل في الفلكة. وكذا قال مجاهد

JISHUMI:v7p4813/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r4.claim: Falak originally means anything circular; examples include a spindle whorl, a rounded breast, the heavenly orbit, and a raised round patch of land.
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r4.anchor: والفلك: أصله كل دائر، وجمعه: أفلاك، ومنه: فلكة المغزل

JISHUMI:v7p4813/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r5.claim: With ḍamma on the first syllable, fulk means a ship and may be singular or plural; its singular may also have the same form as its plural.
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r5.anchor: والفلك بضم الفاء: السفينة، قيل: هو واحد وجمع، وقيل: واحدها: فلك، نحو أسد وأسد

JISHUMI:v7p4813/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r6.claim: Tasbih means declaring God free of every evil; it also means prayer because prayer glorifies God, and Arab usage can use subhana to express astonishment.
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r6.anchor: والتسبيح: التنزيه، ومعنى سبحان الله: براءة له من كل سوء، والسبحة والتسبيح: الصلاة أيضا

JISHUMI:v7p4813/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r7.claim: A poet’s line using سبحان at Alqama’s boast illustrates the expression; another view takes سبحان as astonishment, while swimming and running are related terms.
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r7.anchor: قال الشاعر: أقول لما جاءني فخره ... سبحان من علقمة الفاخر وقيل: معناه عجبا له، والسباحة: العوم

JISHUMI:v7p4813/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r8.claim: The masculine plural يسبحون is used for the heavenly bodies because the action is predicated of them as rational agents, as in the sun and moon appearing to prostrate in 12:4.
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r8.anchor: لأنه أضيف إليها الفعل على تدبير ما يعقل، ونظيره: (والشمس والقمر رأيتهم لي ساجدين)

JISHUMI:v7p4813/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r10.claim: The plural verb follows although sun and moon were just named because all the stars are intended.
JISHUMI:v7p4813/r10.anchor: وقال: يسبحون على الجمع وإن تقدم ذكر الشمس والقمر؛ لأنه أراد النجوم كلها

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r7.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r7.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the falak as the sky.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r8.claim: Another meaning is a revolving circle carrying the sun, moon, and stars; the word is related to the round spindle whorl.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r8.anchor: القطب المستدير الدائر بما فيه من الشمس والقمر والنجوم ومنه سميت فلكة المغزل لاستدارتها

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r9.claim: Al-Mawardi cites a poet's phrase “the revolving falak” as evidence for the word's sense.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r9.anchor: باتت تقاسي الفلك الدوار … حتى الصباح تعمل الأقتار

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r10.claim: The falak's circular motion has been likened to the motion of a ball.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r10.anchor: أحدهما : أنه كدوران الأكرة . الثاني : كدوران الرحى

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r11.speaker: الحسن وابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r11.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj liken the falak's circular motion to a millstone.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r11.anchor: كدوران الرحى قاله الحسن , وابن جريج

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r12.claim: One account identifies the falak as the sky revolving with the sun, moon, and stars.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r12.anchor: أحدها : أنه السماء تدور بالشمس والقمر والنجوم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r13.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r13.claim: Qatada identifies it as a circle in the sky in which stars revolve while the sky remains fixed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r13.anchor: الثاني : أنه استدارة في السماء تدور فيها النجوم مع ثبوت السماء , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r14.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r14.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies it as a circle between heaven and earth in which stars revolve.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r14.anchor: الثالث : أنها استدارة بين السماء والأرض تدور فيها النجوم , قاله زيد بن أسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r15.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r15.claim: Mujahid explains “swim” as move or run through their course.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas explains “swim” as revolve; on this reading, the celestial bodies move within the falak.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p445/r16.anchor: الثاني : يدورون قاله ابن عباس , فعلى الوجه الأول يكون الفلك مديرها

MUJAHID:v1p410#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p410#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p410#2/r1.claim: They run in their orbits like the iron part of a hand mill.
MUJAHID:v1p410#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ في فلك يسبحون ﴾ يقول يجرون كهيئة حديدة الرحى

MUQATIL:21:31-33/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:31-33/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:21:31-33/r5.claim: The sun and moon enter from the west, pass beneath the earth to the east, then travel through the sky to the west; falak means orbit and yasbahun means run, describing their circuit.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r1.claim: Night is for rest and day for activity.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r1.anchor: خلق الليل ﴾ لتسكنوا فيه ﴿ والنهار ﴾ لتتصرفوا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r2.claim: The sun serves as the day’s lamp and the moon as the night’s lamp.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r2.anchor: ﴿ والشمس ﴾ لتكون سراج النهار ﴿ والقمر ﴾ ليكون سراج الليل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r3.claim: The tanwīn in “each” replaces an omitted genitive complement; it means all of them, and the pronoun refers to the sun and moon as classes of celestial bodies.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r3.anchor: التنوين فيه عوض عن المضاف إليه أي كلهم والضمير للشمس والقمر المراد بهما جنس الطوالع

NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the falak is the sky.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما الفلك السماء

NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r5.speaker: الجمهور
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r5.claim: The majority say the falak is an enclosed wave beneath the sky in which the sun, moon, and stars travel.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r5.anchor: والجمور على أن الفلك موج مكفوف تحت السماء تجري فيه الشمس والقمر والنجوم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r6.claim: “They swim” means that they travel and revolve.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r7.claim: The clause “they swim” is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause describing the sun and moon.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p79#4/r7.anchor: والجملة في محل النصب على الحال من الشمس والقمر

QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r11.claim: Night was made for rest and day for people to pursue their livelihoods.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r11.anchor: ذكرهم نعمة أخرى: جعل لهم الليل ليسكنوا فيه، والنهار ليتصرفوا فيه لمعايشهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r12.claim: The sun marks daytime and the moon nighttime, enabling people to know months, years, and reckoning, as explained earlier in al-Israʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r12.anchor: أي وجعل الشمس آية النهار، والقمر آية الليل لتعلم الشهور والسنون والحساب

QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r13.claim: “All” includes the sun, moon, stars, planets, night, and day.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r13.anchor: يعني من الشمس والقمر والنجوم والكواكب والليل والنهار

QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r14.claim: The celestial bodies run swiftly, like a swimmer moving through water; 79:3 and the name for a horse extending its forelegs in a run illustrate the image.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r14.anchor: أي يجرون ويسيرون بسرعة كالسابح في الماء. قال الله تعالى وهو أصدق القائلين:

QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r15.speaker: سيبويه والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r15.claim: Sibawayh and al-Farraʾ explain the masculine plural as treating the celestial bodies as rational beings because they obey like rational beings.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r15.anchor: فمذهب سيبويه: أنه لما أخبر عنهن بفعل من يعقل وجعلهن في الطاعة بمنزلة من يعقل

QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r16.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r16.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says the plural form is used to complete the verse ending.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:32-33/r16.anchor: وقال الكسائي: إنما قال: «يسبحون» لأنه رأس آية

QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r1.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r1.claim: Al-Kisaʾi illustrates his verse-ending explanation with 54:44, which has منتصر rather than منتصرون.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r1.anchor:
نحن جميع منتصر
[القمر: 44] ولم يقل منتصرون.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r2.claim: Another view assigns the running to the orbits, so the verb is attributed to them.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r3.claim: Qurtubi says the soundest view is that the planets move in seven spheres below the layered heavens, which are the domain of angels and the causes of the dominion; the moon, Mercury, Venus, sun, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, zodiac, and greatest sphere occupy levels eight and nine as described.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r3.anchor: والأصح أن السيارة تجري في الفلك، وهي سبعة أفلاك دون السموات المطبقة، التي هي مجال الملائكة

QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r4.claim: فلك is the singular of the stellar spheres; the word derives from rotation, as in the round spindle whorl, and describing a woman's breast as tafallaka means it became rounded.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r4.anchor: وأصل الكلمة من الدوران، ومنه فلكة المغزل لاستدارتها. ومنه قيل: فلك ثدي المرأة تفليكا

QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r5.claim: Abu ʿAmr says أفلاك may be pluralized on the fuʿul pattern, like asad/asud and khashab/khashub.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r5.anchor: قال أبو عمرو: ويجوز أن يجمع على فعل مثل أسد وأسد وخشب وخشب.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿud's hadith compares a horse he left circling to the sphere, whose stars rotate around it.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r6.anchor: وفي حديث ابن مسعود: تركت فرسي كأنه يدور في فلك. كأنه لدورانه شبهه بفلك السماء

QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says the spheres are the courses of the stars, sun, and moon between heaven and earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد: الأفلاك مجاري النجوم والشمس والقمر. قال: وهي بين السماء والأرض.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r8.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r8.claim: Qatada describes the sphere as a rotating circle in the sky that carries the stars while the sky itself remains fixed.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة: الفلك استدارة في السماء تدور بالنجوم مع ثبوت السماء.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r9.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r9.claim: Mujahid compares the sphere to the iron wheel of a mill and its central pivot.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r9.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الفلك كهيئة حديد الرحى وهو قطبها.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r10.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak says the sphere is the celestial body's course and the speed of its movement.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r10.anchor: وقال الضحاك: فلكها مجراها وسرعة مسيرها.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r11.claim: Another view describes the sphere as a contained wave and the course of the sun and moon; God knows best.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:30-33/r11.anchor: وقيل: الفلك موج مكفوف ومجرى الشمس والقمر فيه والله أعلم.

QASHANI:21:33/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:21:33/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:21:33/r1.claim: Night is the soul and day the intellect, illuminated by the spirit's sun and heart's moon; each travels toward God in a rank and station within the spiritual heavens.
QASHANI:21:33/r1.anchor: ليل النفس ونهار العقل الذي هو نور شمس الروح وقمر القلب { كل في فلك } أي: مقر علوي

RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r1.claim: After saying people ignore the sky's signs, Razi details them: sun and moon complete God's favors by producing day and night and benefits through seasonal change and their orbital motions.
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r1.anchor: لما قال : { وهم عن ءاياتها معرضون } فصل تلك الآيات ههنا

RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r2.speaker: جمهور الفلاسفة وأصحاب الهيئة
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r2.claim: Most philosophers and astronomers posit a shared daily motion from east to west and a second, slower west-to-east motion, visible in the planets and inferred for the fixed stars from their changing positions.
