RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r2.anchor: ثم قال جمهور الفلاسفة وأصحاب الهيئة ، وههنا حركة أخرى من المغرب إلى المشرق

RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r3.speaker: جمهور الفلاسفة وأصحاب الهيئة
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r3.claim: Their evidence is that a faster planet passes a slower one eastward after conjunction; the moon's nightly apparent movement away from the sun illustrates this, and fixed stars likewise shift slowly along the zodiac.
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r3.anchor: واستدلوا عليها بأنا وجدنا الكواكب السيارة كلما كان منها أسرع حركة إذا قارن ما هو أبطأ حركة

RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r4.claim: Razi rejects two simultaneous motions of one body in opposite directions: that would require it to be in two places at once; interruption of the spheres conflicts with philosophers' own premises.
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r4.anchor: لزم كون الجرم الواحد متحركا حركتين إلى جهتين مختلفتين دفعة احدة وذلك محال

RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r5.claim: An objection says the eastern motion might stop during western motion and resumes the millstone-and-ant example of opposite movements; Razi replies that uninterrupted spheres are required by the philosophers' own principles and that the analogy cannot overturn his proof.
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r5.anchor: فإن قيل : لم لا يجوز أن يقال : الشمس حال حركتها إلى الجانب الشرقي تنقطع حركتها إلى الجانب الغربي

RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r6.claim: Razi says the evidence for eastward motion is weak: all spheres may move eastward at different speeds, with slower spheres merely lagging, from the outermost and fastest down to the moon; this better fits cosmic order, with earth at rest.
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r6.anchor: أما الذي احتجوا به على أن للكواكب حركة من المغرب إلى المشرق فهو ضعيف

RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r7.claim: The bodies also move in latitude, north and south; without this inclination, effects would be confined to one place or produce permanent extreme seasons, while appropriately paced cycles spread benefit and avoid excess.
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r7.anchor: أما حركاتها في عروضها فظاهرة وذلك بسبب اختلاف ميولها إلى الشمال والجنوب

RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r8.claim: The measured duration of motion in each direction lets the celestial effects mature without excess or deficiency, while the intellect grasps only a little of creation's secrets.
RAZI-FULL:v22p143/r8.anchor: إذا كان هناك ميل يحفظ الحركة في جهة مدة ثم ينتقل إلى جهة أخرى بمقدار الحاجة

RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r1.claim: The plural “they swim” includes stars along with the sun and moon, so the pronoun supplies the plural referent even though stars were not named earlier.
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r1.anchor: لا يجوز أن يقول : { وكل فى فلك يسبحون } إلا ويدخل في الكلام مع الشمس والقمر النجوم

RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r2.claim: In Arabic, falak denotes anything circular, and its plural is aflak.
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r2.anchor: الفلك في كلام العرب كل شيء دائر وجمعه أفلاك

RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r3.speaker: الضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says the falak is not a body but the orbit or track of the celestial bodies.
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r3.anchor: فقال بعضهم : الفلك ليس بجسم وإنما هو مدار هذه النجوم وهو قول الضحاك

RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r4.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r4.claim: Most scholars say the falak is a physical body on which the stars move; Razi says this is closer to the Qur'an's apparent wording.
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r4.anchor: وقال الأكثرون : بل هي أجسام تدور النجوم عليها ، وهذا أقرب إلى ظاهر القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r5.claim: One account describes the falak as a wave held together, in which the sun, moon, and stars run.
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r5.anchor: فقال بعضهم : الفلك موج مكفوف تجري الشمس والقمر والنجوم فيه

RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r6.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi says the falak is gathered water through which the planets swim, reasoning that swimming occurs only in water.
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r6.anchor: وقال الكلبي : ماء مجموع تجري فيه الكواكب واحتج بأن السباحة لا تكون إلا في الماء

RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r7.claim: Razi rejects the claim that swimming must be in water, noting that a horse stretching its forelegs while running is also called a swimmer.
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r7.anchor: قلنا ؛ لا نسلم فإنه يقال في الفرس الذي يمد يديه في الجري سابح

RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r8.speaker: جمهور الفلاسفة وأصحاب الهيئة
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r8.claim: Most philosophers and astronomers describe the spheres as solid bodies, neither heavy nor light, incapable of rupture, joining, growth, or decay.
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r8.anchor: وقال جمهور الفلاسفة وأصحاب الهيئة : إنها أجرام صلبة لا ثقيلة ولا خفيفة غير قابلة للخرق

RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r9.claim: Razi says the spheres' qualities cannot be known except through transmitted reports.
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r9.anchor: والحق أنه لا سبيل إلى معرفة صفات السموات إلا بالخبر

RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r10.claim: Razi lays out three possibilities: a stationary sphere with moving stars; moving spheres and stars, in the same or opposite directions and at varying or equal speeds; or moving spheres with stationary stars fixed in them.
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r10.anchor: فإنه إما أن يكون الفلك ساكنا والكواكب تتحرك فيه كحركة السمك في الماء الراكد ، وإما أن يكون الفلك متحركا

RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r11.speaker: جمهور الفلاسفة وأصحاب الهيئة
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r11.claim: Philosophers reject the first two possibilities because they would rupture the spheres, and settle on stars fixed in moving spheres.
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r11.anchor: فلم يبق إلا القسم الثالث وهو أن يكون الكوكب مغروزا في الفلك واقفا فيه والفلك يتحرك

RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r12.claim: Razi rejects the premise that spheres cannot rupture, says all three arrangements are possible for God, and takes the Qur'an's apparent wording to favor fixed spheres with stars swimming through them like fish in water.
RAZI-FULL:v22p144/r12.anchor: بل الحق أن الأقسام الثلاثة ممكنة والله تعالى قادر على كل الممكنات والذي يدل عليه لفظ القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the tanwin on kull substitutes for an annexed noun, meaning all of them swim in an orbit.
RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r1.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : { كل } التنوين فيه عوض عن المضاف إليه

RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r2.speaker: أبو علي بن سينا
RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r2.claim: Avicenna argues that the planets are living and rational because the masculine rational plural form is used and because Joseph saw the sun, moon, and stars prostrating.
RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r2.anchor: احتج أبو علي بن سينا على كون الكواكب أحياء ناطقة بقوله : { يسبحون }

RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r3.claim: Razi replies that the rational plural is used because the stars are described by an action, swimming; it does not prove that they are rational beings.
RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r3.anchor: والجواب : إنما جعل واو الضمير للعقلاء للوصف بفعلهم وهو السباحة

RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r4.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the clause is either an accusative circumstantial clause attached to sun and moon or an independent resumption with no syntactic slot.
RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r4.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : فإن قلت الجملة ما محلها قلت النصب على الحال من الشمس والقمر أو لا محل لها لاستئنافها

RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r5.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r5.claim: Asked how all can swim in one orbit when each has a separate orbit, al-Zamakhshari compares it to saying the prince clothed them in one robe: each received its own.
RAZI-FULL:v22p145/r5.anchor: فإن قلت : لكل واحد من القمرين فلك على حدة فكيف قيل جميعهم يسبحون في فلك ؟

STUDYQURAN:21:33/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:33/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:21:33/r1.claim: For the elements named in this verse, the commentary directs readers to its discussion of 36:40.
STUDYQURAN:21:33/r1.anchor: For the various elements in this verse, see 36:40c.

STUDYQURAN:21:33/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:33/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:21:33/r2.claim: The image of heavenly bodies gliding in orbits prompts commentators to discuss the cosmology behind it.
STUDYQURAN:21:33/r2.anchor: The notion of heavenly bodies gliding in orbits is an occasion for some commentators to discuss the cosmology underlying this imagery

STUDYQURAN:21:33/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:33/r3.speaker: Q and R
STUDYQURAN:21:33/r3.claim: A common premodern Islamic cosmology held that heavenly bodies moved within spheres made of an ethereal or subtle substance.
STUDYQURAN:21:33/r3.anchor: The common notion in Islamic cosmology during premodern times was that the heavenly bodies moved within spheres of an ethereal or subtle substance (Q, R)

STUDYQURAN:21:33/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:33/r4.speaker: Ḍaḥḥāk
STUDYQURAN:21:33/r4.claim: Ḍaḥḥāk took orbits to mean only the heavenly bodies’ trajectories through the heavens.
STUDYQURAN:21:33/r4.anchor: such as Ḍaḥḥāk, for whom “orbits” meant nothing more than the trajectories of these bodies through the heavens

STUDYQURAN:21:33/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:33/r5.speaker: al-Qurṭubī and al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:21:33/r5.claim: Al-Qurṭubī and al-Rāzī conclude that knowledge of these cosmological matters is available only through revelation.
STUDYQURAN:21:33/r5.anchor: al-Qurṭubī’s and al-Rāzī’s concluding remarks on this verse point out that no one can have knowledge of these matters except through revelation

TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r1.claim: God created night, day, sun, and moon as blessings and evidence of His authority and sole divinity; their alternation serves human livelihoods and worldly and afterlife affairs.
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: {كل في فلك يسبحون} [الأنبياء: 33] قال: فلك كهيئة حديدة الرحى

TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid, as transmitted also by Ibn Jurayj, compares the orbit to an iron disk or ring of a millstone.
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: {كل في فلك يسبحون} [الأنبياء: 33] قال: فلك كهيئة حديدة الرحى

TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the falak is the sky.
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {كل في فلك يسبحون} [الأنبياء: 33] قال: فلك السماء

TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains falak as running and speed.
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r4.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {كل في فلك يسبحون} [الأنبياء: 33] الفلك: الجري والسرعة

TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r5.claim: Another reported interpretation is a contained wave in which the sun, moon, and stars run.
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: الفلك موج مكفوف تجري الشمس والقمر والنجوم فيه

TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r6.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r6.claim: Another group identifies it as the celestial axis around which the stars rotate, citing a rajaz line about the revolving falak.
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل هو القطب الذي تدور به النجوم. واستشهد قائل هذا القول لقوله هذا بقول الراجز [البحر الرجز] باتت تناجي الفلك الدوارا … حتى الصباح تعمل الأقتارا

TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r7.claim: Qatāda says the celestial bodies run in the sky's orbit; Maʿmar transmits the same explanation from him.
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r7.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {كل في فلك يسبحون} [الأنبياء: 33] أي في فلك السماء

TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd locates the orbit between heaven and earth among the paths of the stars, sun, and moon, and reads the constellations verse as placing them between the two, not on earth.
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {كل في فلك يسبحون} [الأنبياء: 33] قال: الفلك الذي بين السماء والأرض من مجاري النجوم والشمس والقمر. وقرأ: {تبارك الذي جعل في السماء بروجا وجعل فيها سراجا وقمرا منيرا} [الفرقان: 61]

TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan compares the falak to a mill or spindle whorl.
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r9.anchor: وذكر عن الحسن أنه كان يقول: الفلك طاحونة كهيئة فلكة المغزل

TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r10.claim: In Arabic falak can mean anything round; several proposed circular forms are possible, but the source gives no decisive proof to specify which one the verse means.
TAB-FULL:v16p264#2/r10.anchor: وذلك أن الفلك في كلام العرب هو كل شيء دائر، فجمعه أفلاك، وقد ذكرت قول الراجز:

TAB-FULL:v16p267/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p267/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p267/r1.claim: Since scripture, prophetic report, or decisive authority does not identify a specific shape, one should say only that the sun and moon each move in a circle and avoid unsupported claims.
TAB-FULL:v16p267/r1.anchor: وإذ كان كل ما دار في كلامها، ولم يكن في كتاب الله، ولا في خبر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ولا عمن يقطع بقوله العذر، دليل يدل على أي ذلك هو من أي

TAB-FULL:v16p267/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p267/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p267/r2.claim: Here يسبحون means that the celestial bodies run or move along.

TAB-FULL:v16p267/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p267/r3.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p267/r3.claim: Mujāhid and Ibn Zayd both gloss يسبحون as running.
TAB-FULL:v16p267/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قوله: {كل في فلك يسبحون} [الأنبياء: 33] قال: يجرون

TAB-FULL:v16p267/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p267/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p267/r4.claim: The masculine human plural ending is used for sun and moon because they are described with human-like actions, as with the sun and moon being seen prostrating in Joseph's dream.
TAB-FULL:v16p267/r4.anchor: فأخرج الخبر عن الشمس والقمر مخرج الخبر عن بني آدم بالواو والنون، ولم يقل: يسبحن، أو تسبح كما قيل: {والشمس والقمر رأيتهم لي ساجدين} [يوسف: 4]

TABATABAI:21:30-33/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:30-33/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:30-33/r8.claim: The verse assigns an orbit to night, day, sun, and moon: night is the conical shadow alongside earth opposite the sun, day is its opposite, and each has its own course.
TABATABAI:21:30-33/r8.anchor: الآية ظاهرة في إثبات الفلك لكل من الليل وهو الظل المخروطي الملازم لوجه الأرض

TABATABAI:21:30-33/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:30-33/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:30-33/r9.claim: These are conditions relative to earth and its atmosphere; the sun and fixed stars shine intrinsically, while the moon and planets reflect light, and their day-night conditions differ from ours.
TABATABAI:21:30-33/r9.anchor: والمراد مع ذلك بيان الأوضاع والأحوال الحادثة بالنسبة إلى الأرض وفي جوها وإن كانت حال الأجرام الأخر

TABATABAI:21:30-33/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:30-33/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:30-33/r10.claim: Sabaha here means moving through water by cleaving it; the plural verb treats the celestial bodies as rational agents, as in other Qur’anic usage.
TABATABAI:21:30-33/r10.anchor: وقوله { يسبحون } من السبح بمعنى الجري في الماء بخرقه

TABRISI:21:31-32/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:31-32/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:31-32/r10.claim: Falak originally means anything circular, such as the whorl of a spindle; the verb can describe a woman’s breast becoming rounded.
TABRISI:21:31-32/r10.anchor: والفلك أصله كل شيء دائر ومنه فلكة المغزل ويقال فلك ثدي المرأة تفليكا إذا استدار

TABRISI:21:31-32/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:31-32/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:31-32/r11.claim: Swimming, floating, and running express motion in this context.

TABRISI:21:31-32/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:31-32/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:31-32/r20.claim: They move or revolve in their orbits; the reference includes the sun, moon, and stars, since night is mentioned.
TABRISI:21:31-32/r20.anchor: أي يجرون. وقيل: يدورون وأراد الشمس والقمر

TABRISI:21:31-32/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:31-32/r21.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:21:31-32/r21.claim: Ibn Abbas says they move through good and evil, hardship and ease.
TABRISI:21:31-32/r21.anchor: وقال ابن عباس يسبحون بالخير والشر بالشدة والرخاء

TABRISI:21:31-32/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:31-32/r22.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:31-32/r22.claim: The plural verb treats the celestial bodies as rational beings.
TABRISI:21:31-32/r22.anchor: وإنما قال يسبحون لأنه أضاف إليها فعل العقلاء

FARRA:v2p201/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p201/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p201/r7.claim: The sun, moon, night, and day take the human-style plural because swimming is an action of people; likewise the sun and moon are سجّد in 12:4.
FARRA:v2p201/r7.anchor: لغير الآدميين للشمس والقمر والليل والنهار، وذلك أن السباحة من أفعال الآدميين

FARRA:v2p201/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p201/r8.speaker: يقال
FARRA:v2p201/r8.claim: It is said that the falak is a contained wave in which celestial bodies run.
FARRA:v2p201/r8.anchor: ويقال: إن الفلك موج مكفوف يجرين فيه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r1.claim: “All” refers to all the heavenly bodies that rise.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r2.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r2.claim: Al-Layth says falak in the hadith usage is the rotation of the sky, specifically the act of revolving.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r2.anchor: قال الليث: الفلك في الحديث (¬6) دوران (¬7) السماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r3.speaker: المنجمون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r3.claim: Astronomers describe seven spheres below the sky, each carrying one of the seven planets at a different height, revolving by God's permission.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r3.anchor: وأما المنجمون فيقولون: سبعة أطواق (¬1) دون السماء قد ركبت فيها النجوم السبعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة، الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda transmits from al-Aṣmaʿī that a falak can be a round, raised part of the land, singular falaka; al-Rāʿī's line describes the resulting raised circular form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r4.anchor: وروى أبو عبيدة عن الأصمعي: الفلك: قطع من الأرض تستدير وترتفع عما حولها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r5.speaker: الراعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r5.claim: Al-Rāʿī's line uses falak muzhar for a rounded rise that appears when lowlands and valleys are feared or exposed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r5.anchor: قال الراعي: إذا جفن هول بطون (¬5) البلاد ... تضمنها فلك مزهر (¬6)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r6.claim: In Arabic, falak can mean anything round; its plural is aflāk, as in a spindle whorl and the rounded shape of a girl's breast.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r6.anchor: والفلك في كلام العرب: كل شيء مستدير، وجمعه أفلاك، ومنه فلكة المغزل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r7.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r7.claim: Al-Suddī says falak means an orbit and a circular path.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r7.anchor: وأما المفسرون، فقال السدي في قوله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r8.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r8.claim: Al-Kalbī says falak is the sky's roundness and, by extension, any circular thing; the stars turn within the round sky.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r8.anchor: وقال الكلبي: الفلك استدارة السماء، وكل شيء استدار فهو فلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r9.claim: Mujāhid compares the orbit to the shape of a millstone; the author explains that stars circle the pole as a millstone turns around its iron spindle.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r9.anchor: وهذا معنى قول مجاهد: كهيئة حديدة الرحى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r10.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r10.claim: Most exegetes say the falak is the circular track that contains the stars.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r10.anchor: وعلى (¬9) هذا معنى قول أكثر المفسرين، قالوا: الفلك مدار النجوم الذي يضمها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r11.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan compares the falak to a mill or a spindle whorl, meaning a rounded track in which the stars run.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r11.anchor: وقال الحسن: الفلك طاحونة [كهيئة فلكة المغزل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd says the falak is between heaven and earth and consists of the paths of the stars, sun, and moon, like the astronomers' spheres.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r12.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: الفلك الذي بين السماء والأرض [من] (¬3) مجاري النجوم والشمس والقمر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r13.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r13.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says falak is the pole around which the stars revolve, but the author rejects this: the word must name the circular container in which they swim.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p64#2/r13.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الفلك: القطب الذي تدور به النجوم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r1.claim: Yasbaḥūn means they move swiftly like swimmers; the verb can also describe a horse extending its forelegs in a run, as in al-Aʿshā's verse, and 79:3 calls stars swimmers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r1.anchor: أي: يجرون بسرعة كالسابح في الماء، وقد قال في موضع آخر في صفة النجوم: {والسابحات سبحا}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r2.speaker: الأعشى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r2.claim: Al-Aʿshā's line “a swift, spirited horse” illustrates calling a running horse a swimmer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r2.anchor: ومنه قول الأعشى: وسابح ذي ميعة (¬1) ضامر (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r3.claim: Some assumed swimming only applies in water and therefore made the falak a water wave for stars; al-Farrāʾ reports this view, which the author calls mistaken.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق، أبو عبيدة، الفراء، المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r4.claim: The masculine rational plural is used because these bodies are described with a rational action; Abū Isḥāq, Abū ʿUbayda, al-Farrāʾ, al-Mubarrad, and linguists cite akalūnī al-barāghīth; the line of al-Jaʿdī and 12:4 illustrate the construction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r4.anchor: قال أبو إسحق: قيل {يسبحون} هو كما يقال لما يعقل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r5.speaker: الجعدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r5.claim: Al-Jaʿdī's line illustrates the plural verb marking in the expression “the stars of the Great Bear drew near and descended.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p67/r5.anchor: وأنشد للجعدي: تمرزتها والديك يدعو صباحه ... إذا ما بنو نعش دنوا فتصوبوا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:31-35/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:31-35/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:31-35/r4.claim: The celestial bodies run and travel; a falak is the orbit of the stars.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r9.claim: Qatadah says the sun, moon, and night and day move in the orbit of the heaven.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r10.speaker: عوف البكالي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r10.claim: ʿAwf al-Bakali says the sky is dome-shaped and the sun, moon, and stars run in an orbit beneath it, not attached to it; he also locates Jerusalem twelve miles from the sky and al-Ubulla farthest away.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r10.anchor: عن أبي صالح، عن عوف البكالي قال: إن السماء خلقت مثل القبة، وإن الشمس والقمر والنجوم ليس منها شيء لازق

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r11.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAmr says the sun and moon face the sky and turn their backs toward earth, illuminating both; he cites 71:15–16 about the moon among the heavens and the sun as a lamp.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r11.anchor: عن قتادة، عن شهر بن حوشب، عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: إن الشمس والقمر وجوههما إلى السماء، وأقفاؤهما إلى الأرض

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r12.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAmr says the sun is in the fifth heaven in winter and the seventh in summer; when challenged that it appears in the lowest heaven, he says it could not remain there if that were so.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p309#2/r12.anchor: قلت لعبد الله بن عمرو: ما بال الشمس تصلانا أحيانا وتبرد أحيانا؟ قال: أما في الشتاء فهي في السماء الخامسة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r1.speaker: الأعمش
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r1.claim: Al-Aʿmash says the sun is brought nearer to earth in winter for people to benefit from it and raised in summer so its heat will not harm them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r1.anchor: الحسن، عن صاحب له، عن الأعمش ذكره بإسناده قال: إن الشمس أدنيت من أهل الأرض في الشتاء لينتفعوا بها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r2.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r2.claim: Mujahid explains yasbaḥūn as revolving like the spindle of a spinning wheel.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r2.anchor: عن أبي يحيى، عن مجاهد قال: {يسبحون} [الأنبياء: 33] يدورون كما يدور فلك المغزل.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r3.speaker: ابن مجاهد عن أبيه
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r3.claim: Ibn Mujahid, quoting his father, explains the motion as running like the iron of a millstone.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r3.anchor: وتفسير ابن مجاهد، عن أبيه: {يسبحون} [الأنبياء: 33] ، يجرون كهيئة حديدة الرحى.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r4.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r4.claim: Al-Hasan’s tafsir places the sun, moon, and stars in a mill-like orbit between heaven and earth; they would not run if fixed to the sky.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r4.anchor: وفي تفسير الحسن: إن الشمس والقمر والنجوم في طاحونة بين السماء والأرض كهيئة فلك المغزل

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r5.speaker: الكلبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi explains yasbaḥūn simply as “they run.”

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r6.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r6.claim: Mujahid explains the sun and moon’s ḥusbān in 55:5 as motion like a mill’s rotation.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p311/r6.anchor: أن مجاهدا قال في قوله: {الشمس والقمر بحسبان} [الرحمن: 5] قال: حسبان كحسبان الرحى.

ELMALILI:21:33/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:33/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:33/r1.claim: The celestial bodies move through their orbits; the verse does not say that a rotating sphere carries them around.
ELMALILI:21:33/r1.anchor: Demek ki zannedildiği gibi onları felek döndürüyor değil, onlar felekte ve her biri bir felekte yüzüyorlar

ELMALILI:21:33/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:33/r2.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:21:33/r2.claim: Some take falak to mean a rotating thing and accordingly imagine it as a revolving physical sphere; Elmalılı says this reflects the science of their time.
ELMALILI:21:33/r2.anchor: “Felek” devreden şey demek olduğuna göre bazıları feleği bir cism-i devvâr addetmişlerdir

ELMALILI:21:33/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:33/r3.speaker: Dahhâk
ELMALILI:21:33/r3.claim: Dahhak defines falak as the orbit or place where a celestial body revolves, a purely mathematical description.
ELMALILI:21:33/r3.anchor: Dahhâk’ten rivayet olunduğu üzere “felek” nücûmun medârı, yani devrettiği mahal

ELMALILI:21:33/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:33/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:33/r4.claim: Elmalılı notes that medar and the newer term mahrek designate a place of revolution or motion.
ELMALILI:21:33/r4.anchor: “medar” kelimesi gibi “mahrek” demek de ıstılah olmuştur. Biri “devr”den ism-i mekân, biri de “hareket”ten ism-i mekândır

ELMALILI:21:33/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:33/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:33/r5.claim: Although only sun and moon are named, the plural yasbahun is noteworthy because it signals more than two subjects.
ELMALILI:21:33/r5.anchor: haberde tesniye getirilmeyip de ikiden ziyadeyi ifade eden cemi‘sîgasıyla يَسْبَحُونَ buyurulması şâyân-ı dikkat görülmüştür

ELMALILI:21:33/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:33/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:33/r6.claim: One explanation supplies the omitted stars after sun and moon, with all referring collectively to the three.
ELMALILI:21:33/r6.anchor: Birisi والشمس والقمر والنجوم takdîrinde olmasıdır ki Şems ü Kamer’in yanında nücûm hazf edilmiş, sonra da kül ve cem‘ile hepsine işaret olunmuş demektir

ELMALILI:21:33/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:33/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:33/r7.claim: Another explanation treats sun and moon as names for a class of stars or celestial bodies.
ELMALILI:21:33/r7.anchor: İkincisi bu karîne ile Şems ü Kamer’den cins-i nücûm kast edilmiş olmasıdır

ELMALILI:21:33/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:33/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:33/r8.claim: Within that generic reading, Elmalılı prefers taking sun and moon as encompassing all stars, some of which resemble moons, rather than leaving the other stars unmentioned.
ELMALILI:21:33/r8.anchor: sâir yıldızların da kimisi Kamer mânasında olduğuna işâreten bu ikisini hepsinin cinsi gibi ahzetmek daha münâsibdir

ELMALILI:21:33/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:33/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:33/r9.claim: A further possibility is that kull includes the previously mentioned earth along with sun and moon, so every body has its own orbit.
ELMALILI:21:33/r9.anchor: “kül” ta‘mîmi Şems ü Kamer’le beraber mâkablinde zikri geçen Arz’ı dahi ihtivâ ederek hepsine işaret olmak da muhtemildir

ELMALILI:21:33/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:33/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:33/r10.claim: Whatever the grammatical reading, Elmalılı says the verse overturns the old astronomy in which spheres were thought to move the sun and moon, and accords with bodies moving in space along their own axes or paths.
ELMALILI:21:33/r10.anchor: Zira onlar Şems ü Kamer’i felek hareket ettiriyor diyorlardı. Burada ise her birinin birer felekte kendilerinin yüzdükleri haber veriliyor

ELMALILI:21:33/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:33/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:33/r11.claim: When a scientific theory appears to conflict with the Quran, one should not bend the Quran to science; science should be reconciled with the Quran.
ELMALILI:21:33/r11.anchor: Kur’ân’ı fenne uydurmaya çalışmamalı, fenni Kur’ân’a tevfik etmeye uğraşmalıdır

ELMALILI:21:33/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:33/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:33/r12.claim: The ordered, continuous motion of every celestial body, each on its own course and safely suspended, displays God's artistry, power, and oneness; unbelievers nevertheless turn away and attribute it elsewhere.
ELMALILI:21:33/r12.anchor: hepsi muallakta, hepsi yolunda, hepsi nizâmında, hepsi mahfuz yüzüyorlar da yüzüyorlar. Bu ne bedî‘sanat, ne büyük kudret

ELMALILI:21:33/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:33/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:33/r13.claim: The scientific teaching of the verse, alongside the earlier sign of earth's separation from heaven, is a divine sign of Muhammad's prophethood: Copernicus, Newton, or Laplace could discover the principle, but an unlettered Prophet's announcement of it before the world's sciences is miraculous evidence.
ELMALILI:21:33/r13.anchor: bunu ümmî bir fıtratın bütün cihân-ı fenne karşı bir makām-ı tehaddîde haber verivermiş olması onun nübüvvetini meydana koyan

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r1.claim: These verses offer evidence for God’s oneness, uniqueness, and limitless power to recreate the universe and its creatures after they perish.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r1.anchor: Allah’ın birliğini, ortağı ve benzerinin bulunmadığını, bu evren ve içindeki varlıklar yok olduktan sonra onları yeniden yaratabilecek sonsuz güce sahip bulunduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r21.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r21.claim: The cited cosmic signs serve life: night provides rest, day enables work and livelihood, the sun gives Earth heat and light, and the moon reflects enough sunlight to serve living beings in darkness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:30/r21.anchor: Bunlar canlıların sükûnet içerisinde dinlenmelerini sağlayan gece, çalışıp geçimlerini sağlamalarına vesile olan gündüz, ısı ve ışınlarıyla dünyayı aydınlatan ve ısıtan güneş

BURHAN:v3p240/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p240/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p240/r1.claim: Arabic convention commonly places night before day, including in Qur'anic expressions and calendar dating by nights, even though day is masculine and would normally prevail in coordination.

BURHAN:v3p240/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p240/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p240/r4.claim: The sequence putting the heavens and earth before darkness and light, then the sky before night, day, sun and moon, reflects the priority of place over time in creation.

BURHAN:v3p240/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p240/r5.speaker: الطبري
BURHAN:v3p240/r5.claim: Al-Tabari cites reports from Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurayra to argue that earth and the sun or light were created before night and day, which are names for periods measured by the sun and moon's motion.
BURHAN:v3p240/r5.anchor: وقد صرح بها الإمام أبو جعفر الطبري في أول تاريخه

NAHHAS:v3p69/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p69/r2.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v3p69/r2.claim: Sībawayh says the plural human ending is used because the heavenly bodies are described with a verb of rational beings and are treated as obedient rational beings.
NAHHAS:v3p69/r2.anchor: مذهب سيبويه أنه لما خبر بفعل من يعقل وجعلهن في الطاعة بمنزلة من يعقل خبر عنهن بالواو والنون

NAHHAS:v3p69/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p69/r3.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p69/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains يسبحون by saying their actions are described with human actions.
NAHHAS:v3p69/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء لما خبر عنهن بأفعال الآدميين قال يسبحون

NAHHAS:v3p69/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p69/r4.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v3p69/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says the plural form closes the verse, as in نحن جميع منتصر.
NAHHAS:v3p69/r4.anchor: وقال الكسائي يسبحون لأنه رأس آية كما قال ﴿ نحن جميع منتصر ﴾

RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r3.speaker: الغزالي
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r3.claim: Al-Ghazali sides with the sphere because sensory evidence cannot be contradicted; any relevant report may be interpreted, and scripture does not explicitly require flatness but points toward circularity at 21:33.
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r3.anchor: والغزالي رحمه الله قال نحن نوافقهم في ذلك فإن لهم عليها دليلا من المحسوسات

BURHAN:v3p306/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p306/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p306/r2.claim: Nonrational beings take pronouns and forms used for rational beings when they are represented as speaking or acting like humans; the author extends the explanation to the listed examples.
BURHAN:v3p306/r2.anchor: لما أخبر عنها باخبار الآدميين جرى ضميرها على حد من يعقل وكذا البواقي

BURHAN:v4p317/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p317/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p317/r7.claim: When no complement appears, it is understood; scholars differ whether its tanwin substitutes for the complement or is ordinary declension.
BURHAN:v4p317/r7.anchor: وربما خلا من الإضافة لفظا وينوي فيه

BURHAN:v4p321/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p321/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p321/r5.claim: The plural verb in كل في فلك يسبحون cannot describe each sun, moon, night, or day as a plural; al-Zamakhshari’s estimate كل أحد in a related example supports the analysis.
BURHAN:v4p321/r5.anchor: إن كلا من الشمس والقمر والليل والنهار لايصح وصفه بالجمع

BURHAN:v3p151/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p151/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p151/r9.claim: Deleting the genitive complement alone is relatively uncommon; examples include كل في فلك, فضلنا بعضهم على بعض, and لله الأمر من قبل ومن بعد.
BURHAN:v3p151/r9.anchor: وهو أقل استعمالا كقوله ﴿ كل في فلك يسبحون ﴾

ITQAN:v3p268/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p268/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p268/r9.claim: Inanimate entities can be treated grammatically as rational beings, as in the stars prostrating and celestial bodies swimming.
ITQAN:v3p268/r9.anchor: الخامس والعشرون إجراء غير العاقل مجرى العاقل نحو ﴿ رأيتهم لي ساجدين ﴾ ﴿ كل في فلك يسبحون ﴾

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r18.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r18.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r18.claim: Some ordering follows temporal priority: jinn before humans, drowsiness before sleep, ʿĀd before Thamūd, night before day, and darkness before light; jinn's earlier creation is stated in 15:27.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p29/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p29/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p29/r3.claim: Night precedes day because darkness existed before the celestial bodies, and the sun precedes the moon; darkness is likewise placed before light.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p29/r3.anchor: فقدم الليل لأنه أسبق من النهار وذلك لأنه قبل خلق الأجرام كانت الظلمة وقدم الشمس على القمر لأنها قبله في الوجود

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p480/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p480/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p480/r5.claim: Night precedes day and darkness preceded the celestial bodies; the sun is placed before the moon because it existed first.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p480/r5.anchor: فقدم الليل لأنه أسبق من النهار وذلك لأنه قبل خلق الأجرام كانت الظلمة وقدم الشمس على القمر لأنها قبله في الوجود

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبرجلحسنأبواهوأحسنأب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبرجلحسنأبواهوأحسنأب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبرجلحسنأبواهوأحسنأب.claim: Celestial bodies and ants take rational-style agreement because the text depicts them as obeying, prostrating, or acting like beings that understand; such wording blocks treating them as ordinary inanimates.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبرجلحسنأبواهوأحسنأب.anchor: أنه بمنزلة ما يعقل ويسمع لما ذكرهم بالسجود
